title: LAUA: Handling Missing Modalities and Unpaired Data in Multimodal Federated Learning

problem.claim: Multimodal federated learning must operate with missing or unpaired modalities and cross-modal heterogeneity across clients, which can hinder stable optimization.

gap.claim: Existing methods often rely on paired supervision or uniformly treat client updates, making them brittle under modality missingness and client-level variability.

contributions.claim: LAUA is a federated multimodal learning framework for a mixture of unimodal and multimodal clients.
LAUA aligns representations in a shared variational latent space and uses KL regularization to provide a confidence signal for estimating uncertainty.
LAUA combines client-side self-supervised learning, task supervision, internal distillation, and server-side uncertainty-weighted aggregation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across various datasets, LAUA substantially mitigates performance degradation under modality missingness for retrieval and regression tasks.
LAUA attains up to 20% relative improvement in MRR for retrieval and up to 24.3% relative improvement in MSE for regression.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal federated learning trains collaboratively from distributed multimodal data while preserving privacy.
Missing or unpaired modalities and cross-modal client heterogeneity hinder stable optimization, while existing mitigation methods have brittle assumptions.
LAUA supports mixtures of unimodal and multimodal clients using shared latent representations, self-supervision, task supervision, and internal distillation.
The server adaptively down-weights unreliable client updates using uncertainty-weighted aggregation.
The authors report reduced degradation under modality missingness and relative gains on retrieval and regression tasks.

source_observation.claim: KL regularization in a shared variational latent space provides a lightweight confidence signal, which is then used for uncertainty-weighted aggregation.

interpretation.claim: A model-derived uncertainty signal can connect representation learning with adaptive weighting of distributed updates.

application.claim: In heterogeneous federated systems, consider weighting client updates according to an explicitly estimated reliability signal.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the uncertainty signal is calibrated or reliable across all client distributions.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, or absolute metric values.
The abstract does not specify the degree of modality missingness, client heterogeneity, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or independent verification of the reported improvements.
